security_privacy_cost_impact:
SUBSTANTIAL, AND IT IS WHERE EVERY ROLE RUN SPENT ITS TIME. One new tenant table, ENABLE + FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, one SELECT policy on active membership and one RESTRICTIVE narrowing four joins deep (snapshot -> post -> send -> intent -> item). A1 measured tenant isolation closing in BOTH directions for all nine fixture identities, 17 write attempts refused across three distinct layers, and the per-column ACL exactly as claimed: authenticated reads 8 columns and writes none, app_worker reads 8 and inserts 6, anon holds nothing, relacl is NULL so there is no hidden PUBLIC grant, and no role at all holds UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE or REFERENCES.

THE CLASSIFICATION DECISION THIS BATCH TURNS ON: `metrics` is PROVIDER-3 and sits INSIDE the client projection (question D), so the control is a SHAPE and not a projection. A1 threw 28 attacks at it -- nested objects, arrays, numeric strings, Thai unicode, case-variant and Cyrillic-homoglyph keys, jsonb scalars -- and no provider-authored TEXT reached app. It then found what did: a NUMERIC external post id passed all four type-discriminating constraints and was readable by an ordinary client, while batch 120 withholds even the HASH of one from the same role. Closed by a magnitude bound (A0's number, owed to the Owner). Q0 then found that the constraints themselves were undefended -- widening the allowlist by one key let a Graph API error sentence through with every layer green -- and that is closed by pinning the key set BY TEXT in the migration and again in the fixture.

Cost: negligible. One table, two indexes, no new role, no new grant to any existing role beyond this table, and no external call anywhere.
migration_and_data_impact:
ONE MIGRATION AND ONE FORWARD KEY ON A MERGED TABLE. 121_publisher_metrics.sql creates app.performance_snapshots (8 columns, 7 constraints, 2 indexes, 2 policies, no trigger and no updated_at), and adds published_posts_scope_unique to batch 120's app.published_posts.

THE FORWARD KEY IS THE PART A REVIEWER SHOULD LOOK AT FIRST. app.published_posts carried no unique on (workspace_id, business_profile_id, id), so the composite scope FK every other child in this schema uses could not be written against it. Migration invariant 1 forbids rewriting 120, so the key is added here -- 111's shape on 110's table and 120's on 081's. It was reported to the Owner BEFORE the work as question H, not discovered during it. A reader of 120_publisher.sql will see a table whose scope key is not there; the comment on the constraint says which batch added it and why.

NO DATA MIGRATION AND NO BACKFILL: the table is new and empty. Nothing in this repository can write to it -- no client role holds INSERT and the service is refused at the policy layer -- so it will stay empty until RFC-2026-022 §7 holds and a command surface exists.
